regions.name: Louisville / North Central
regions.headline: Metro pilots, health systems, civic tech, logistics, startups, and public AI convenings.
regions.summary: Louisville is KYAI's densest civic and institutional signal lane: city government, UofL, health systems, logistics employers, accelerators, and recurring public technology rooms.
regions.nextWin: Turn TALK AI Day, UofL digital innovation, health, logistics, and local government signals into a public city brief.
openQuestions: Which public agencies are actively evaluating AI procurement?
What health-system AI work can be translated into public education?
Which local events should KYAI use as recurring signal-review rooms?

regions.name: Lexington / Bluegrass
regions.headline: University research, agriculture, health, public-sector pilots, and student pathways.
regions.summary: The Bluegrass lane is anchored by research institutions, student talent, agricultural AI, healthcare research, and policy activity near Frankfort.
regions.nextWin: Map university labs, applied AI programs, faculty work, student projects, and agriculture-related AI pilots.
openQuestions: Which AI courses and certificates should be tracked each semester?
Which faculty projects have a public-facing Kentucky benefit?
How should KYAI distinguish research discovery from deployable community tools?

regions.name: Western Kentucky
regions.headline: Data centers, energy, logistics, agriculture, manufacturing, river industry, and local workforce.
regions.summary: Western Kentucky is becoming a high-stakes AI infrastructure and workforce region, with data center, power, manufacturing, and community-impact questions moving fast.
regions.nextWin: Build a source-backed data center and power-impact watchlist people in the region can understand and challenge.
openQuestions: Which public meetings and tax commitments need monitoring?
What local jobs are construction-only versus permanent operations?
Which communities need plain-language explainers on data center impact?

regions.name: Eastern Kentucky / Appalachia
regions.headline: Rural access, digital readiness, small-business workflows, workforce transition, and public trust.
regions.summary: The Appalachia lane should make AI practical and trustworthy for counties where access, workforce transition, broadband, and local institutions matter more than hype.
regions.nextWin: Package a practical AI basics session for Appalachian small businesses, libraries, churches, and workforce partners.
openQuestions: Which community rooms can host trusted beginner sessions?
Where can AI help with paperwork, grants, customer service, and fraud prevention?
What barriers should be documented before recommending new tools?

regions.name: Northern Kentucky
regions.headline: Cincinnati-adjacent talent, logistics, advanced manufacturing, startups, and campus pathways.
regions.summary: Northern Kentucky can connect cross-border technology activity back into a Kentucky-specific AI map for employers, schools, students, and founders.
regions.nextWin: Connect Cincinnati-adjacent AI events, employers, NKU programs, and manufacturing activity back into KYAI.
openQuestions: Which cross-border events should be treated as Kentucky-relevant?
What employer training is already happening but not publicly visible?
Which NKY organizations should be listed first?

regions.name: South Central Kentucky
regions.headline: Career pathways, manufacturing, small business, community colleges, and public workshops.
regions.summary: South Central Kentucky needs a practical AI lane connecting Bowling Green, schools, workforce partners, manufacturers, and small businesses.
regions.nextWin: Track applied AI activity around Bowling Green, schools, manufacturing employers, and regional workforce partners.
openQuestions: Which schools and employers are already experimenting with AI?
What starter workshops would be most useful to local teams?
How should KYAI surface student projects and pathway programs?
